strengths: Novel problem formulation: Extends spatial understanding from single images to multi-frame settings, addressing an important gap for robotics and embodied AI applications

Comprehensive experimental validation: 36% average improvement over base model; strong generalization to held-out benchmarks (BLINK, ERQA, CVBench-3D); scalability analysis demonstrating consistent gains with data and parameters; maintains general VQA capabilities without forgetting

Well-designed task definitions: Five complementary tasks (depth, correspondence, camera motion, object motion, object size) grounded in Structure-from-Motion and covering fundamental spatial capabilities

Interesting empirical findings: Multi-task synergy with cross-dataset transfer; preliminary evidence of emergent spatial abilities requiring model size threshold; practical robot learning demonstrations showing out-of-distribution generalization
Excellent reproducibility: Detailed algorithms (BFS, clustering), hyperparameters, extensive supplementary material with data samples; well-justified evaluation metrics
